newsitem.title: USA: US conservation voters' group targets congressmen.
newsitem.headline: US conservation voters' group targets congressmen.

text.p: The League of Conservation Voters (LCV) Wednesday added six Republican office-seekers to a list of politicians it has targeted in upcoming elections.

The league, a political arm of environmental groups, in Senate races targeted Sen. Larry Pressler, seeking re-election to his South Dakota seat; Gordon Smith, a state senator running to fill the seat being vacated by Oregon Sen. Mark Hatfield, and Representative Jim Lightfoot, running against incumbant Iowa Sen. Tom Harkin.
In House races, it targeted North Carolina Representative Fred Heineman, Washington Representative Randy Tate and Maine Representative Jim Longley.
The league previously named five congressmen to its "dirty dozen" list and said it will name the last one soon.

An LCV spokesman said there is "an embarrassment of riches" of candidates for the final slot, and the league is taking a little longer to make sure it uses its resources in a race where they would be most effective.

Previously named to the list were Republican Reps. Helen Chenoweth of Idaho, Michael Flanagan of Illinois, Frank Riggs of California and Steve Stockman of Texas, as well as Democratic Representative Gary Condit of California.
"We're urging people to vote against the dirty dozen candidates in November because they all have clear records against the environment," league president Deb Callahan said at a news conference.
